en.h: A 256-acre (104 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Huntingdon County, 12 miles (19 km) south of State College. Man-made 22-acre Whipple Lake was built at the height of the late 19th-century lumber era to power a sawmill. The land was bought from the Iroquois Confederacy in 1754; later the Monroe Iron Works ran there, making charcoal and mining iron ore, and remnants of the mines can still be seen.
